utterances.text: Isn't it right that whenever the Serb authorities are taken to task with the massacres in Srebrenica, they reply with allegations of crimes committed against them in the Srebrenica area? MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, objection sustained. Why are you putting these questions, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's the motive for the forgery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness hasn't conceded any forgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there re-examination, Mr. Di Fazio or not? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Radojicic, that brings your testimony to an end here. On behalf of my two colleagues, Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser, and also on behalf of myself, forming this Trial Chamber, and on behalf of the Tribunal in general, I would like to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and you will now receive all the assistance you require from our staff to facilitate your return back home at the earliest possible. You finished today in advance so you will probably return home a day in advance which I am sure you will agree to. On behalf of everyone present here, I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me address you on something which necessarily we have to come to sooner or later. You will recall that when we first discussed the Rule 98 bis business here, you remember when I spent about half an hour or three-quarters of an hour, not more, addressing you on how this new system will work, we had agreed initially that there will be more or less one week less on your side to prepare for your intervention, sort of another week, Prosecution side. Then, as you know, we had further business to -- to transact following that, and we were anticipating that our decision would follow more or less in the week following the week starting on the 20th. So -- and the week starting on the 27th, end of the month, anyway, end of the month. Of course, that has all changed now. As I take it, by the 3rd of June, all submissions relating to Rule 98 bis will be over. There will only be further submissions if in our deliberations we feel that we require your help in addressing some further issue, which may or may not occur. But the bottom line is that while we were anticipating previously a month ago that we would hand down the decision at the end of the month, at the end of June, we will now hand the decision, unless we encounter difficulties, more or less as soon as you come over from the special course that you have to attend to. So basically we are talking of the 8th or the 9th but anyway, that week. That week this process of the Rule 98 bis motion will be over. Now, we will be the last ones to anticipate what the outcome of the Rule 98 bis exercise is going to be. We don't know, obviously, because we have discussed, we have discussed a lot, but we've still got a lot to discuss and we have not heard your submissions which may change our approach for all that matters, either side. But we have to take both assumptions, and the assumptions are three. We could decide that the case will proceed on all counts. We could decide that the case stops on all counts. And we could decide that the case proceeds on some counts and -- but not on others. Assuming for the time being, just for organisational purposes, and for no other purpose, that we will decide either that the case continues on all counts or that the case continues on some counts and not that we will hand down a decision of acquittal on all. I'm not excluding it but we can't really discuss progress if we take it into consideration. So forget that for the time being and assume that it will be either one or the other. Then we are no longer talking of a period of time of roughly three weeks which would have justified what I had stated earlier on, namely the case for the defence will start after the break, after the recess, because I would have understood you, Madam Vidovic, and you, Mr. Jones, standing up and saying we need more than two weeks, three weeks, in order to be able to start presenting our case. This time, there will be practically, for all intents and purposes, if we hand down the decision on the 9th or on the 10th of June, you have a month and a half. You have a month and a half. During which time, if there is a decision which is partially or totally against you, under the Rule 98 bis regime, we can plan or we will need to plan how the Defence is going to proceed. But my message that I am trying to convey is as follows: That although I cannot say, and neither of us can, what our decision is going to be, we have a responsibility to prepare, well in advance, in case our decision is totally or partially against your client. So be also prepared and start the machine in motion to more or less organise yourself and be able to come back to the Trial Chamber and tell us what your plans are, assuming that you will at least, as far as certain issues or certain areas, that you will cover in defending your client are concerned, which could possibly be dealt with before we go into recess. And then, of course, if the case continues in whole or in part, obviously we will need to deal with the bulk after the recess but be prepared to come back with some practical suggestions as to how to utilise at least part of the period, the month and a half plus, that we will have before the recess begins on the 22nd, 23rd of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I just ask for one clarification in that respect? Your Honour will recall when we discussed this before that we were keen obviously to know whether we needed witnesses here in July, because obviously it takes a huge amount of planning and it does depends on which charges remain. Sorry, can you just give us a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's precisely for that reason I'm clarifying, as I understand Your Honour it would be a question of us in July coming back with some planning, some planning hearing or something of that nature, a Pre-Defence Conference, but not actually having physically witnesses present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, this is not what I mean. I mean exactly the opposite. I mean exactly that you ought to be prepared to bring forward witnesses before the recess. At least you should be able to identify at least some areas, some areas in your defence or line of defence that you will be adopting, and try to address those areas by means of witnesses before we start the recess. In other words, we will need to plan because much depends on what we are going to decide on the -- following the Rule 98 bis because as I said we are not in a position, not even -- not to tell you but not to know ourselves what we are going to decide. And obviously if there is a decision to proceed with the case in part, or in whole, I mean then your defence has to be organised accordingly. Certain areas that you may have planned for in the past already for your defence may need not to be addressed if we decide partially to acquit, while they would need to be addressed if we decide to continue with the case in toto. So I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's simply to say that may be problematic for us because so far we haven't been planning for July and there are things happening in June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you need to start planning for July. This is -- at least, let's put it like this. I mean, there will be definitely a meeting immediately after the decision, the Rule 98 bis decision, all right? There will definitely be a 65 ter meeting with both of you to organise the rest. That's if there is no decision of acquittal because if there is a decision of acquittal obviously we are not talking of any further meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I Your Honour just reserve the opportunity to confer with my colleague and then speak to you about our concerns about witnesses in July. And then also, just before I forget, as far as the 98 bis schedule is concerned, I did have a brief exchange of words with Mr. Wubben this morning about any possible reply on either party's part and I understand from what Your Honour was saying that possibly the following week there might be a need for clarifications or for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May be, I'm not excluding anything, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What I want to suggest is simply that on the Friday, if it were a question of a short period of time for Your Honours just to seek clarifications from each side by way of reply, then that would -- that would be something which we would be in favour of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. My intentions definitely and I would imagine I have the agreement of my colleagues there, would be to conclude submissions on that Friday, on the 3rd. Then, of course, we come back to you if -- if, for example, let's say that we get an indication from the Prosecution that according to them, the charge under count 4 and 6 is proven by this or that piece of evidence, for the purpose of Rule 98 bis, and upon verification, we see that this must be a clear mistake, then we might decide to overlook it completely and ignore what is being submitted by the Prosecution. Or come back to you, reconvene sitting, and say, Mr. Di Fazio, Mr. Wubben, where are you seeing it? Because we applied a microscope and couldn't see an iota of what you're suggesting there. So at the end of the day it may happen like that. It may not happen because we don't know as yet, obviously. But the thing is this, that previously it would have made sense to tell you, you don't need to worry about starting your Defence until after the recess because we would have heard basically three weeks and three weeks is too short a time to expect you to prepare. The other thing -- but now it's different. Now you have a good month and a half plus. The other thing that you need to prepare for is that you know more than I do that the Rules provide for the opportunity of your client to make a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We are aware of that Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course I am not going to ask you whether your client has decided to make a statement or not, and what's the decision on whether there have been consultations but I would suggest that you keep this in mind, because if that is going to happen, my preference is to have that statement before you proceed, then, with the rest of the evidence and not leave it to later. I cannot force it on your client, obviously, but I do think I owe it to your client and to you in particular that in my opinion it would carry much more weight if it's given before rather than after.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And if I could just reiterate we do have grave problems possibly starting in July. I won't enter into it now. It's really -- it's something that perhaps my colleague would -- would better address you on in terms of the overall planning of our -- of our case but rather than going into that now, if Your Honours would give us the opportunity to consider among ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. But it was more or less to put you in the picture. Don't put the Trial Chamber in a position where it has to justify the unjustifiable. In other words, carrying over the case for the defence to after the recess because there was a mere three-week space that wouldn't have been questioned by anyone, but carrying the case for the Defence to after the recess when there is more than a month and a half will be questioned by everyone because not even in the big cases did we give a month and a half. All right? So otherwise, if certain -- if you have certain particular problems, we will address them, but be prepared to start the Defence case before the recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we'll discuss it and alert you to particular problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's nothing to do with you so I'm not inviting you to comment, Mr. Wubben, unless you really want to comment. Thank you. So we stand adjourned till the day after tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of May, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25
